$comment: Machine-readable version of docs/data-request/README.md. Written for the Behind the Jersey data agent. Everything here is a request, not data: never copy a value from this file into the dataset unless the same value is in the website seed with a source.
summary: The website renders every page from 14 normalised JSON files: clubs, kits (one per club per season or period, with the sponsors and where they sit on the shirt), sponsors, owners (with parent chains up to a state), claims (one sourced statement each), deals (money), changes, dropped, leagues, sports, levels, tiers, contacts and meta. The per-team files in Beyond-The-Jersey/data don't have seasons, placements, owner chains, sourced claims, changes or tiers yet, and several clubs the designs depend on have no sponsors at all. Please publish the normalised files next to the per-team files.

target.howToCheck: pip install jsonschema && python3 validate.py normalized/   (copy validate.py and the schema/ folder next to it, or run it from a checkout of the website repo). It must print OK. Warnings about missing source URLs are allowed but should go down over time.
target.keepPerTeamFiles: Yes. Keep data/*.json and index.json if anything else uses them. The website only reads normalized/.

rules: Never invent a fact, number, source, URL, rating, deal value or contact detail. Unknown stays null (with a note saying what is missing) or is left out.
Every claim, deal value, change, dropped item and contact channel needs a source object {name, date, url}. url may be null only while it is being looked up; add a note saying so.
Wikipedia and Wikidata are leads, not sources. Follow them to the primary document (club announcement, official report, named press article) and cite that.

The website derives each club's blood level (Clean, Spotted, Stained, Soaked) from its sponsors' tiers and placements. Don't publish a club level or blood_meter. Only set kits[].levelOverride if a person decided an exception.

Sponsor tiers are unrated, none, concern, serious, severe (see tiers.json). Don't map the A to F grades onto them. A sponsor stays tier 'unrated' until its owner chain and claims are sourced and a person has reviewed them.
Ids are ASCII kebab-case: atletico-de-madrid, not atlético-de-madrid. For clubs, sponsors and owners that already exist in the website seed, keep the seed id so links don't break.
Seasons are 'YYYY-YY' (2026-27). Calendar-year leagues use 'YYYY'. One kit per club per season, or per period when nothing changed across several seasons (like Arsenal 2006-07 to 2017-18).
Where your data and the website seed disagree, keep the value with the better and newer source, and list every such change in the PR description.

fieldMapping.how: Also fill shortName, code (3 letters), aliases (nicknames fans type, e.g. 'spurs', 'gunners').

Seed id if the club is in the seed, otherwise ASCII kebab-case of the name. Examples: bournemouth → afc-bournemouth, brighton-hove-albion → brighton-and-hove-albion, atlético-de-madrid → atletico-de-madrid, fc-schalke-04 → schalke-04, los-angeles-rams → la-rams, málaga-cf → malaga-cf.
soccer → soccer, basketball → basketball, american_football → american-football, baseball → baseball (new; add it to sports.json with status 'not-mapped').

premier_league → premier-league, laliga_easports → la-liga, bundesliga → bundesliga, nba → nba, nfl → nfl, mlb → mlb (new; add to leagues.json with clubCount 30). Set league status to 'partial' once any of its clubs has a rated sponsor.
The country the club plays in: England, Spain, Germany, USA, Canada.

fieldMapping.to: sponsors.json (one entry per company, shared across clubs) + kits.json → sponsors[] {sponsorId, placement, source}
fieldMapping.how: category shirt_sponsor/jersey_sponsor usually means placement 'front'; check it. Sleeve, back and shorts sponsors each get their own entry. The kit's season comes from the source, not from the date the scraper ran.
Trace the owner chain: Emirates → Government of Dubai (via Investment Corporation of Dubai) → United Arab Emirates. ownership is 'owned' or 'part-owned'.
Don't convert. Assign the tier from tiers.json definitions once the owner's claims are sourced and reviewed. Until then tier 'unrated' and status 'unrated' (or 'being-rated').
One factual sentence about who pays, like 'Paid for by a government that UN experts say has 3,000–4,000 troops fighting alongside M23 rebels in eastern Congo.' null when unrated.

fieldMapping.to: deals.json → value {amount, currency, unit, per, upTo, usdApprox} + source
fieldMapping.how: Only with a named source and date. usdApprox uses $1 = £0.75 = €0.87. Unknown value: value null (the site shows 'value not disclosed').

fieldMapping.to: source {name, date, url} on the kit sponsor, deal, claim or change
fieldMapping.how: See rules: cite the primary document.
true only when a person checked the claim against its source.

One entry per club with channels [{type, value, label, source}]. Each channel needs the URL of the club page where it is published. Drop placeholders (+44 800 XXX XXXX) and addresses that were generated from the slug (marketing@<slug>.com). Leave a channel out if you can't source it.
The designs rate shirts by sponsors, not club owners. Keep them in the per-team files.
Date of the latest real data change (YYYY-MM-DD), shown on the landing page.

For items about an organisation rather than a club (orgName set, clubId null): the league or competition id, so the site can show them under the right sport. Examples in the seed: Basketball Africa League deal → basketball-africa-league, Haas F1 × Uralkali → formula-1, UEFA × Gazprom → uefa.

presentationFields.note: Some kit fields exist only for the team-page design. Copy them from the seed for the three designed clubs and leave them out for other kits.

fields.kits[].photos: Paths like assets/shirts/<club-id>/<season>-home-front.jpg. The image files live in the website repo (public/assets) because they aren't cleared for public use yet. Don't add images to the data repo.
fields.kits[].sponsors[].side: 'front' or 'back': which photo the logo is on.
fields.kits[].sponsors[].hotspot: {x, y, w, h}: logo centre and size as fractions of the 720×800 photo.
fields.kits[].sponsors[].cardSlot: 'L', 'R' or 'T': where the sponsor card sits around the shirt.
fields.kits[].summary: One plain sentence for the team page, e.g. 'Saudi Arabia’s state fund pays for the front of this shirt. Rwanda’s government pays for the back.' null if nobody has written one.
fields.kits[].change: {kind: worse|better, text, badge} when the shirt got worse or better than the previous period.
fields.clubs[].crest: Path to a crest in the website repo (assets/crests/<club-id>.png) or null. The site shows initials when null.
fields.clubs[].hasTeamPageDesign: Deprecated and optional. The site decides from the kit.
